senses.gloss:
Mūta in the later Saṃhitās and the Brāhmaṇas^1 denotes a
‘woven basket.’ Mūtaka means a ‘small basket.’^2
1) Kāṭhaka Saṃhitā, xxxvi. 14; Taittirīya Brāhmaṇa, i. 6, 10, 5; Lāṭyāyana
Śrauta Sūtra, viii. 3, 8.
2) Śatapatha Brāhmaṇa, ii. 6, 2, 17.

Mūtiba appears in the Aitareya Brāhmaṇa^1 as the name of
one of the barbarous peoples enumerated as nominally Viśvā-
mitra's outcast offspring. The Śāṅkhāyana Śrauta Sūtra^2
gives the name as Mūcīpa or Mūvīpa.
1) vii. 18, 2.
2) xv. 26, 6.
Cf. Muir, Sanskrit Texts, 12, 358,
483.
